purpose: Catch a race condition where switching the drawer's eventId while a slower fetch for the previous event is still in flight would otherwise let the stale response overwrite newer history.
preconditions: Frontend: Vitest + Testing Library with a controllable, manually-resolved mocked getEventHistory API so request completion order can be sequenced independently of request start order.
steps: Render EventAuditDrawer open for event 42 and let getEventHistory start an unresolved fetch.
Rerender the same drawer instance with eventId changed to 99 while the first fetch is still pending, starting a second fetch.
Resolve the second (event 99) request first and confirm its history renders.
Resolve the first (event 42, stale) request afterwards and confirm its history is discarded, not applied over the current event's rendered history.
data: Two mocked getEventHistory responses for events 42 and 99, resolved out of start order (99 resolves before 42)
expected: Only the latest request's history is ever rendered; a stale response resolving after a newer one must not overwrite the currently displayed history.
actual: Added a monotonically-increasing request-id guard in EventAuditDrawer's fetchHistory so only the response matching the latest request is applied to state; the new '[CONFLICT] ignores a stale fetch response when eventId flips mid-fetch' test (client/src/components/EventAuditDrawer.test.tsx) passed, and EventAuditDrawer.tsx retained 100% statement/branch coverage (16/16 tests in file; 647/647 in full client suite).
